body:
## Ask

The platform substrate the commercial features (#86, #88) and the marketplace (#90) stand on:

**Identity & accounts**
- Users, SSO (OIDC/SAML), account storage, payment methods and history
- Payments integration wired to the milestone billing in #88

**Operations & governance**
- **Config boards** — the .vibey-gh.toml-style configuration surfaced as editable boards,
  so an operator manages a fleet without hand-editing TOML across repos
- **Reporting dashboards** — delivery throughput, phase timings, estimate-vs-actual (#88),
  spend, margin trend
- **User roles** — operator / engineer / client / bot, least-privilege by default
- **Log tracing** — a delivery traceable end to end across the six phases and every repo it
  touched, one correlation id
- **Security auditing** — who did what, when, with which authority; append-only; the
  bypass-actor and token lessons from vibey-gh#130/#131 written into the design

## Doctrine boundary

Accounts are for the **hosted, commercial platform**. The FOSS toolchain never grows an
account requirement: every repo in the family keeps working standalone, offline from this
platform, with no sign-in — full capability, forever. If a feature only works with an
account, it belongs to the hosted layer and must have no hook inside the free tools.

## Sequencing

Roles + audit trail first (they gate everything else being trustworthy), then SSO/accounts,
then payments, then boards/dashboards on top of data that by then exists.

## Triage — 2026-09-17 (`develop` @ f2467910, v0.8.0)

**Status: NOT STARTED** · size **XL** · confidence high

**The ask, as read:** Build the hosted-platform substrate: users/SSO/accounts/payments, config boards, reporting dashboards, user roles, end-to-end log tracing on one correlation id, and append-only security auditing - with no hook back into the free tools.

### What already ships
- Log tracing, ledger half: one uuid5-derived correlation id per delivery, wired through bootstrap.py into every BUILD handler and the design/review/deploy/project ledgers (PR #184). This is the one bullet of the seven that is genuinely live in production paths.
- The append-only ledger itself predates the issue (ADR-0003, src/vibey/domain/ledger.py, migrations/0002_event.sql) and gives the audit bullet a substrate - but it records delivery events, not who-did-what-with-which-authority.

### Evidence in the tree
- src/vibey/domain/correlation.py:1-27 - the module docstring names this issue: 'one delivery left behind ten unrelated ids ... (issue #89)'. DeliveryCorrelation derives a uuid5 id keyed on the project alone; landed as commit 687c1aa7 'feat(domain): one correlation id per delivery, traceable end to end (#184)'
- src/vibey/domain/interfaces/correlation_interface.py exists beside it, satisfying ADR-0016
- Production-reachable: src/vibey/bootstrap.py:375,391,405 compose BuildImplementHandler / BuildVerifyHandler / BuildIntegrateHandler, and :615,639,643,644 compose PostgresProjectRepository, PostgresDesignLedger and PostgresReviewLedger - all of which write the derived id (build_implement_handler.py:206,270; build_verify_handler.py:308,393,436; build_integrate_handler.py:149,278; build_engine_run.py:43; design_ledger.py:44; review_ledger.py:52; project_repository.py:93)
- src/vibey/infrastructure/logging.py:170-182 - the log-line half is explicitly NOT live: 'Nothing in production enters this scope yet ... today's log lines still carry no correlation_id.' CorrelationLogContext is built and tested but never entered, because it needs an application-side port and a binding in the composition root
- src/vibey/cli/main.py:153 correlation_id=uuid4() inside _build_spend_recorder, which is called from the live `vibey work` path at main.py:363 and the live `vibey worker` path at main.py:1364 - DESIGN BudgetSpent events still get a random id and cannot be joined to the delivery
- src/vibey/infrastructure/otel.py (TelemetryTracer, Span) is imported only by tests/infrastructure/test_otel.py - nothing under src/ imports it, so it is dead code, not shipped tracing
- …and 6 more

### What is actually left
- Wire CorrelationLogContext into production: add an application-side port for it, bind it in bootstrap.py at the WorkerLoop job-execution boundary, so log lines carry correlation_id (src/vibey/infrastructure/logging.py:170-182 names exactly this gap)
- Fix src/vibey/cli/main.py:153 - thread the DeliveryCorrelation through _build_spend_recorder so DESIGN BudgetSpent events join the delivery instead of minting uuid4()
- Decide src/vibey/infrastructure/otel.py's fate: wire it into bootstrap.py or delete it - today it is tested dead code that reads as shipped tracing
- Add an actor/authority field to LedgerEvent (or a separate audit stream) and adopt vibey_bootstrap's ChainedAuditRecord rather than hand-rolling one - ADR-0017 makes reuse the default and vibey currently imports nothing from vibey_bootstrap
- Design and migrate the identity schema: users, accounts, roles (operator/engineer/client/bot, least-privilege by default), sessions - none of these tables exist
- Implement SSO (OIDC/SAML) and account storage behind the hosted boundary, with a conformance test proving the FOSS toolchain still runs with no sign-in
- Implement payment methods and history, wired to the milestone billing in #88
- Build config boards: a read/write surface over the .vibey-gh.toml-shaped configuration across the fleet, reconciled from the repository per ADR-0018 rather than replacing it with a settings page
- …and 15 more

### Blockers
- No HTTP API exists in the conductor, so boards and dashboards have no surface to render against
- Payments depend on the milestone billing in #88, which I did not audit
- The doctrine boundary is a real design constraint, not a formality: every table and every hook added here must be provably absent from the free path, which argues for a separate workspace member rather than new modules inside src/vibey

> ⚠️ **Verdict corrected by the verifier.** Six of the issue's seven bullets (users/SSO/account storage, payment methods+history and the #88 billing wiring, config boards, reporting dashboards, user roles, security auditing with actor+authority) have ZERO implementing code, verified by repo-wide grep over *.py/*.yaml/*.sql/*.toml excluding .vibey/worktrees: the only 'oidc' hits are Azure workload-identity for DEPLOY TARGETS (tests/domain/test_deployment_domain.py:30, src/vibey/application/deploy_design_handler.py:55), and the only 'rbac' hits are Kubernetes RBAC for the operator ServiceAccount (deploy/helm/vibey/templates/operator.yaml:9,36,42). migrations/ holds 11 files (0001_project.sql..0011_deployment_stage_set_phases.sql) with no user, account, role, payment-method or audit table. The seventh bullet (log tracing) is half-done by the code's own disclosure. Two decisive reasons the 'partial' verdict overstates: (1) The issue's doctrine boundary states accounts belong to the hosted commercial platform and 'must have no hook inside the free tools'. The one thing the auditor counts as live -- the uuid5 correlation id -- is a ledger-hygiene defect fix INSIDE the free tool (src/vibey/domain/correlation.py, landed as `feat(domain)` in 687c1aa7/PR #184), which merely cites #89 as motivation in its docstring. It is categorically not the hosted substrate the issue asks for. (2) The issue's explicit sequencing is 'Roles + audit trail first (they gate everything else being trustworthy)' -- both are at exactly zero, so nothing that gates the rest has begun. Additionally, two of the auditor's evidence claims are factually wrong: 'wired through bootstrap.py into every BUILD handler' is false -- `grep -n -i correlation src/vibey/bootstrap.py` returns ZERO hits; the deriver reaches production only via module-level default arguments (build_implement_handler.py:78, build_verify_handler.py:167, build_integrate_handler.py:62, build_engine_run.py:36, design_ledger.py:21, review_ledger.py:25, project_repository.py:62), never through the composition root. And there is no 'deploy ledger' -- bootstrap.py:330-331 and :644 construct PostgresReviewLedger with a phase override. Even the 'ledger half' the auditor credits is still broken in a live path (cli/main.py:153 uuid4()) and does not satisfy the bullet's 'every repo it touched' clause, since the id is keyed on project alone (domain/correlation.py:63-65) and nothing in schema or code joins repositories to a delivery.

**Notes:** The issue's own sequencing (roles + audit first) has been inverted by what actually shipped: tracing landed first, roles and audit have not started. Sequencing-wise the cheap wins left are the two correlation gaps (the logging port binding and the main.py:153 uuid4 leak) - both S, both closing a half-finished bullet that the code itself documents as half-finished.

## Audit status — 2026-09-19

**Status: NOT STARTED · planning size: XL**

Correlation and audit plumbing do not constitute the requested hosted identity and operations platform. The current tree has no product-level HTTP surface for SSO, accounts, payments, roles, configuration boards, dashboards, or hosted tracing/audit administration.

Audited at `130afa0449fdcc65833f54ede596f0b4e45a145e`; this issue remains open. This comment supersedes older automated status notes.
